programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents a night at the Royal Albert Hall in tribute to the legendary trumpeter who would have celebrated his centenary in 2026. The concert, in front of a packed audience, combines the musician’s influences – works by Rodrigo and Gershwin – with his own hits from classic albums such as Porgy and Bess, Sketches of Spain and Miles Ahead, amongst others. Acclaimed American jazz trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire joins the BBC Concert Orchestra and Miho Hazama for a celebration of a jazz legend.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Newborn elephant calf Maya and her mother Zadie face many challenges in Kenya.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: A little furry animal from the jungles of South East Asia, called a tree shrew, has attracted great interest from scientists because it shows how a great group of animals may have originated - the mammals. David Attenborough looks at some of the huge variety of mammals. Bats number over a thousand species, many hunt insects, some sip nectar, drink blood, and even catch fish. Contrast those which use sonar with the great whales that sing, the star-nosed mole and the giant anteater, and the potential variations become dramatically clear.

programme.title: Hidden Wales: Last Chance to Save
programme.desc: Writer and adventurer Will Millard returns with more of Wales’s hidden wonders as he explores some of the country’s forgotten historic buildings. In Wales, we are in danger of losing vital pieces of history that tell us who we once were. Beautiful buildings that are architectural gems but also some of the most endangered in the UK. These extraordinary structures, which can give us vital insights into how we once used to live, are in danger of disappearing forever. From extravagant mansions to a 500-year-old farmhouse, crumbling chapels to a massive military fort, and from spectacular industrial sites to a stunning 19th-century theatre, Will travels the length and breadth of Wales to find some of our most vulnerable old buildings, telling their incredible histories and meeting the passionate individuals who are trying to rescue them before it is too late.

programme.title: Kabul
programme.desc: Gilles reluctantly negotiates with the Taliban to arrange the evacuation of refugees by bus. Meanwhile, Giovanni struggles to get his first plane of Afghan refugees off the ground, facing resistance from the Americans who control the airport. Vera tracks down Milad, one of General Hassan’s soldiers, who leads her to a Taliban camp where the general is allegedly being held. Amina finally decides to flee the hospital but turns back to take Nooria with her. They rush toward the French embassy, but they arrive too late - the convoy has already left, aided by Mohammad, a Taliban fighter who demands to be taken with them. Meanwhile, Fazal, now working for the Americans, resumes his undercover identity to infiltrate an Isis cell.

programme.title: Kabul
programme.desc: The French embassy’s convoy moves through Kabul, carrying Zahara and Mohammad - whom she had sentenced to prison just a year before - hidden in the boot of a car. Meanwhile, Isis prepares an attack against the convoy, and Fazal and the Americans race to stop it. Vera is captured in the Taliban camp with General Hassan, and together they devise a plan to escape. Amina and Nooria, left behind after missing the convoy, are arrested by the Taliban but later encounter a commander who unexpectedly decides to escort them to the airport. At Abbey Gate, Giovanni, struggling to manage the chaos, teams up with Joe, an American soldier, to locate his refugees. In the turmoil, he rescues a young Afghan boy, only to realise the child has lost his parents in the crowd.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Class-based sitcom. Audrey takes DeVere to task for failing to turn up in church on Sunday, but then fails to practise what she preaches.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Sitcom. Hyacinth's plans to buy a small weekend retreat in the country take an unexpected turn, and Richard has an unexpected fall.

programme.title: The Bridge: Fifty Years Across the Forth
programme.desc: A unique amateur film provides the centrepiece of a documentary celebrating the 50th anniversary of one of Scotland's great landmarks, the Forth Road Bridge. The documentary traces the memories of the people who built the bridge, the biggest of its kind in Europe at the time, as well as those who ran the Forth ferries that stopped running when it opened in 1964.

programme.title: Deep Down and Dirty: The Science of Soil
programme.desc: For billions of years, our planet was devoid of life, but something transformed it into a vibrant, living planet. That something was soil. It's a much-misunderstood substance, often dismissed as 'dirt', something to be avoided. Yet the crops we eat, the animals we rely on, the very oxygen we breathe, all depend on the existence of the plant life that bursts from the soil every year. In this film, gardening expert Chris Beardshaw explores where soil comes from, what it's made of and what makes it so essential to life. Using specialist microphotography, he reveals it as we've never seen it before - an intricate microscopic landscape, teeming with strange and wonderful life forms. It's a world where the chaos of life meets the permanence of rock, the two interacting with each other to make a living system of staggering complexity that sustains all life on Earth. Chris explores how man is challenging this most precious resource on our planet and how new science is seeking to preserve it.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: For the wildlife and people who live amongst the epic scenery of the Lake District, life is one of continuous change. Cutting-edge camera techniques give a new and unique perspective on a turbulent year in the life of England's largest national park. Time-lapse photography shows months and weeks passing in seconds - snow and ice giving way to sunshine or the frequent rain showers - whilst the animals, plants and people find extraordinary ways to cope with the challenges of this stunning, ancient landscape.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Two concertos under the spotlight. Star soloist Fleix Kleiser makes a dazzling return to the Proms stage playing Mozart's endearing Third Horn Concerto. Making her Proms solo debut, Amy Harman performs the world premiere of Thea Musgrave's 'Out of the Darkness' Concerto for Bassoon. The Academy of St Martin in the Fields brings three heavyweights of the classical repertoire – Elgar, Britten and more Mozart. Britten's playful Simple Symphony sits alongside Elgar's lesser-known Romance for Bassoon and Orchestra, and Mozart's infamous 'Haffner' Symphony. Dancing rhythms ricochet throughout the programme with a light-footed spring between these five pieces. Presented by Georgia Mann from the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: What has the BBC ever done for me?
programme.desc: Romesh asks the big question on an epic journey with a host of famous faces.

programme.title: Secret Knowledge
programme.desc: Through interpretations of some of the archaeological treasures of the Swedish National Museum, now on display in Edinburgh, Dr Janina Ramirez of Oxford University explores the fascinating wealth of Viking culture and its long-lasting influence on the British Isles.

programme.title: Copenhagen: A Prologue with Michael Frayn
programme.desc: Michael Frayn, award-winning playwright and author, introduces the television dramatisation of his highly successful play Copenhagen. He explores why a meeting between two physicists 60 years ago continues to fascinate audiences today. The answer to this question touches on the most significant event of the 20th century: the atom bomb and who would get it first - Hitler or the Allies.

programme.title: Copenhagen
programme.desc: Adaptation of Michael Frayn's award-winning drama, based on a pivotal meeting in 1941 between physicists Niels Bohr and Werner Heisenberg, whose work together had paved the way for the building of the atomic bomb but who now found themselves on opposite sides in the war.

programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks To...
programme.desc: Mark Lawson talks to the distinguished playwright and novelist Michael Frayn about his life and 50-year career. In this reflective interview Frayn discusses the craft of writing farce, fiction and film, the childhood tragedy that has underpinned his life and how his next novel 'will probably be the last nail in my coffin'. Since his early days as a newspaper reporter Frayn has carved a versatile career in novels, plays, philosophy, memoirs, screenplays, translations, farce, tragedy, verse and drama. He has garnered countless awards for his work applauding the wit of Noises Off, the intellectual agility of Copenhagen and the tenderness of Spies. As he continues to write in his seventies, he remains one of our most prolific and respected writers.

programme.title: Reputations
programme.desc: Intimate portrait of Sir John Betjeman, the UK's poet laureate from 1972 until his death in 1984 and one of the most popular English poets of the 20th century. Betjeman's life was full of contrasts. He entertained the world with his warmth and enthusiasm, but, inwardly, he was haunted by fear, religious doubt, remorse and guilt. Highlighting his achievements as a conservationist and broadcaster, the film features contributions from the Prince of Wales and Lord Snowdon.

programme.desc: Sir John Betjeman, poet laureate, visits and explains the architecture of various churches in the Diocese of Norwich. Among the churches he visits are Sandringham church on the Queen's private estate, the Holy House of Our Lady of Walsingham and Norwich Cathedral.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The death of Cambridge academic Jason Arday has prompted intense debate about media conduct, following weeks of reporting on allegations of plagiarism and questions about aspects of his life story. Critics have accused journalists of contributing to an atmosphere of relentless scrutiny, while others argue that legitimate public interest questions were being pursued. Nick Clark, a childhood friend of Jason Arday, reflects on his experience of speaking to reporters. programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Is the space economy the next gold rush? Elon Musk's SpaceX has sparked the public's imagination after its recent stock market debut, but what will all the money being thrown into the space industry actually achieve? The founder of leading investment firm Space Capital, Chad Anderson, explains how what happens in orbit is increasingly important to the economy down on Earth. Ben Thompson also hears from the head of the UN's Office for Outer Space Affairs, Aarti Holla-Maini, about how space law is keeping up with an industry that is moving at breakneck speed. Also on the programme, the billionaire founder of New Zealand-based Rocket Lab, Sir Peter Beck, shines a light on what the private sector can achieve in space and whether SpaceX are friends or rivals.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Anna is in the cultural heart of Ireland, Galway, with her guide, international sporting legend Bundee Aki. Regarded as one of the world’s greatest rugby players, New Zealand-born Bundee has embraced Galway since moving there with his family. He needs Anna's help to improve his cooking skills. Bundee wants to learn to make a family dish, and Anna is up for the challenge. Anna heads off to meet a farmer producing organic beef and then the pair go to work on a high-welfare egg farm.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams target golden gavels as today’s show comes from Nottinghamshire, home of legendary outlaw Robin Hood. Natasha Raskin Sharp meets master bowyer Keith Gascoigne, who shows her how to make a long bow. Keith has been making bows for 62 years. Some of them have helped to win gold at the Paralympics. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Amy is trapped and running out of time, but will assistance arrive too late? On land, Kirsten chases down the traitor’s accomplice. When the traitor on Vigil puts their plans into action, the crew are forced to fight for their lives.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Wendy paints a portrait of Lee's late father, Frank, and gives it to Lee and Lucy as a present. She is expecting them to love it, but that would require the painting to be not just competent but good. Once it’s hanging on their wall, Lee and Lucy must contrive to lose the painting without Wendy or Geoffrey noticing.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: When Lee accidentally sends a rude text about Anna to Lucy, he makes the stupid mistake of sending it to Anna herself. Lee and Lucy now face the impossible task of stealing Anna's phone and deleting the text before she reads it.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lee makes no effort to talk to other parents in the playground, and Lucy is worried that he is becoming isolated and friendless. She fires him up to go into school and make some new friends. Reluctantly Lee gives it a try. He opens up with strangers and makes friends with another lone male, Keith. But Keith is even less sociable than Lee.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Confined to a wheelchair, his right leg encased in plaster after knee surgery, Lee has too much time on his hands, which he uses to watch the world go by through a pair of high-powered binoculars. He soon realises that all is not well in his neighbour’s house opposite. In fact, he is quickly convinced that something despicable is going on.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lee does jury service and joins 11 other jurors to debate whether the accused is guilty or not. A simple enough task - until Lee decides to put the other jurors on trial.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lee organises a family camping trip in an attempt to bring the generations together. But even though he has remembered to bring his guitar for campfire sing-songs, he's forgotten to check the weather. And when Lucy finds something in the woods that looks very much like a human bone, the unhappy campers cannot wait to leave.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Sports mockumentary about GB Paralympian Darren Silverstone, who stole the hearts of a nation before his infamous chokey-o in Tokyo. For the first time, he tells his story - and starts his glorious comeback. In Tokyo 2020, Darren Silverstone was the Paras GB poster boy. (He was on yoghurts, too.) He cruised to the final and charmed the nation along the way with his signature dance move, the dazzle. But as he took that final bend ready to take gold, Silverstone lost his head and celebrated too soon - and in the process, became a national figure of fun. His subsequent journey in the public eye brought approval and consternation in equal measure: from those unforgettably self-deprecating betting adverts to his turn on The Masked Singer as Breadbin. Darren’s best friend and pilot rider in Tokyo, little Paul Potter, was never seen again in the public eye. The two haven’t spoken since. And now, Silverstone’s back. Ready to take to the tandem at Paris 2024. But is he ready? Who will he be riding with? This is I Am Darren.

programme.title: Vigil
programme.desc: Amy confronts one of the crew with her discoveries about their deception, but with her mental health suffering, questions are asked about her fitness to investigate. On land, Kirsten refuses to bow to pressure from the authorities and has concerns that they are orchestrating a cover up. Amy uncovers terrifying new information about someone aboard Vigil. Kirsten closes in on the killer, but their capture reveals the grave threat that Vigil faces.

programme.desc: Steve Backshall and his long-suffering crew return for more deadly encounters with animals hoping to earn a place on his hallowed Deadly 60 list. He and his crew have a nerve-racking close encounter when they are chased by a group of ravenous, three-metre-long komodo dragons, the world's largest venomous lizards! Steve also demonstrates the incredible gliding technique of a tiny flying lizard and heads out on a nocturnal hunt for the beautiful but lethal green pit viper.

programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson and Richard Hammond are on location with the Sweeney movie as they take charge of shooting the film's climactic car chase. Clarkson uses his expertise to choreograph the stunt driving whilst Hammond directs the movie's lead actors, Ray Winstone and Plan B, and organises an explosive finale. Back at the test track James May casts a suspicious eye over the new Vauxhall Corsa VXR Nurburgring and gives his verdict on the brand new Fiat Panda. Plus Hollywood actor Ryan Reynolds is the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.desc: The Piris take refuge in grumpy Millie the Squid’s cave during a storm but accidentally damage a painting. Can they find a clever way to fix it before Millie finds out?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: After a storm passes overhead, many creatures turn up in surprising places and need Cosima and Big Lizard's help. But try as they might, the friends can't find poor Rex.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings blame Weasy for eating the entire supply of popcorn, but he insists it wasn't him! Victim of an injustice, Weasy sets up a trap to find out who the real thief is and prove his innocence.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: The Dumping Ground
programme.desc: Growing up in a care home brings all sorts of tough challenges, but these kids know that if they stick together, they can get through anything life throws at them.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don continues his extraordinary journey to see the world through 80 of its most inspiring gardens with a visit to the United States of America. His plan is to see how America expresses its vast wealth and incredible energy through its gardens. And at a time when the USA is grappling to define its environmental goals, Monty inevitably hopes to find a powerful movement towards sustainable gardening. Beginning in New York, where garden guerrillas are creating community gardens from derelict land, he then travels south to Virginia to visit a garden that reflects the birth of the nation's relationship with the land. Finally, he travels west to California to see if gardens there reflect more than the glitz of the movie industry.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, move to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. The family's safari camp reopens after the rainy season, but Saba's worst nightmare is turning into reality. She has a houseful of guests on their way, the cupboards are bare, and there's nowhere for them to sleep. Husband Frank has problems of his own. He must fit a tracking device to a six-ton bull elephant, but the mission does not go according to plan.

programme.title: The Third Man
programme.desc: Classic film noir about an American writer who visits postwar Vienna to see an old friend but is told that the latter is dead. Incredulous at the suggestion his friend was a criminal, the writer attempts to clear the dead man's name but soon finds events taking a strange turn.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Children’s Week. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers tackle a children’s tutu. In the Transformation Challenge, sustainability is key as the sewers repurpose fleece into stuffed animal toys with adorable results. Finally, mini models are welcomed into the sewing room for the Made-to-Measure Challenge. The sewers are tasked with creating an outfit for their very own superhero creations. Who will handle it like child’s play, and who will be sent to the naughty step?

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The sand-sculpting competition kicks off on St Andrews Beach as seven teams race to create seaside-inspired masterpieces in just six hours, before the tide sweeps in. From nostalgic caravans to cheeky seagulls, creativity meets chaos under the watchful eyes of judges Sadie and Jamie. Who will wow and who will wash out in this high-stakes battle against nature?

programme.title: We Dive at Dawn
programme.desc: World War II drama about a mission to hunt and destroy a dangerous German battleship in the Baltic, which goes wrong when the British submarine Sea Tiger runs short on fuel. A crew member with a flair for the German language is forced to disembark on an enemy-occupied Danish island.

programme.title: Gymnastics: European Championships
programme.desc: Coverage of the men's apparatus finals from the 2026 European Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb, Croatia.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Sheffield, where experts Thomas Plant and James Lewis have their work cut out for them with hundreds of people bringing their items along to be inspected and valued. Thomas is interested in a set of watercolours of industrial Sheffield, and James finds a Victorian automaton. Paul explores the story of the Great Exhibition of 1851, the biggest event of its kind in the world. He also has the chance to get on the pitch of Sheffield FC, the world's oldest football club.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: TV talk show host Matthew Wright and his old pal, stand-up comic Shazia Mirza, travel around the Essex coast. These famous friends have an eco-friendly, electric-powered 1966 Mercedes to take to the road, and the patter is second to none. They’re guided along their journey by expert dealers David Harper and Steven Moore, who try to help them hunt out a profit. In the shops, Matthew embraces his personal passions and is hooked by fishing equipment, while Shazia leans into her playful side, veering towards a few gaming and sporty items. They also explore the local seaside pier, enjoying candyfloss and Ferris wheels. But which of our relic rookies will be victorious in the game at auction?

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The world’s greatest classical music festival pays tribute to soul icon Marvin Gaye with a night of hits including I Heard It Through the Grapevine, What’s Going On and Sexual Healing. The BBC Concert Orchestra lead the celebrations under the baton of Edwin Outwater, featuring the silky vocals of American singer Luke James alongside other special guests. Presented by Andi Oliver from the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: Marvin Gaye: Greatest Hits - Live in Amsterdam 1976
programme.desc: A classic performance recorded on Marvin Gaye’s first European tour in 1976, capturing the legendary soul singer at his unparalleled best. Filmed at Jaap Edenhal in Amsterdam before a sell-out audience, this show is one of the rare live performances captured on film and now preserved for posterity. Featuring 23 classic songs including You’re a Wonderful One, You, It Takes Two and Ain’t No Mountain High Enough.

programme.title: Diana Ross at the BBC
programme.desc: Prepare for a musical chain reaction with an hour lit up by one shining moment after another in this celebration of the best BBC performances from soul legend Diana Ross. From The Supremes to some of her most supreme solo hits, this collection from the archives underlines exactly why Ms Ross has been one of the biggest and most enduring names in music. With songs like Baby Love, I’m Still Waiting and Why Do Fools Fall in Love? from Diana’s visits to the BBC on programmes like Top of the Pops, Wogan and the National Lottery show, this is a must for all fans that promises to leave them Upside Down and enjoying a massive Love Hangover.

programme.title: A Night of Wonder
programme.desc: A studio concert featuring one of the enduring stars of popular music, Stevie Wonder. The show, filmed in 1995, features many of his greatest hits.

programme.title: Motown Master: Lamont Dozier at the BBC
programme.desc: A celebration of the work of songwriter Lamont Dozier, who passed away in 2022, featuring a rich selection from the BBC’s archive of performances of his work from over the decades. As one of the legendary Holland-Dozier-Holland trio, Lamont helped create the Motown sound that spread right across the globe in the 1960s. It set a new standard in popular songwriting, which won over fans like Bob Dylan and The Beatles, with songs like You Keep Me Hanging On, Baby Love, This Old Heart of Mine and Reach Out I’ll Be There. This collection features Dozier’s best-loved and most recognisable hits, performed by artists like Diana Ross and the Supremes, The Four Tops, and Martha and the Vandellas, whom he helped turn into international stars. Plus those who have kept his work alive and relevant to this day, including Phil Collins, Kylie Minogue, Rod Stewart and Rag'n'Bone Man.

programme.title: Motown at the BBC
programme.desc: To mark the 50-year anniversary of Motown in 2009, a compilation of some of the iconic record label's greatest names filmed live in the BBC studios. Visitors from Hitsville USA over the years have included Smokey Robinson and the Miracles, Diana Ross and the Supremes, the Temptations, Stevie Wonder, The Four Tops and The Jackson 5.

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: No longer having to impersonate his twin brother and following his successful closure rate for the major investigation team, puzzle setter John ‘Ludwig’ Taylor returns under his new job title of crime scene consultant. After retrieving the files from storage, John is determined to find the incriminating information that led to Sinclair’s death and James’s disappearance. As the Cambridge Police Authority undergoes investigation in light of the Holly Pinder scandal, an unusual double confession at the theatre sees John take centre stage, where he must prove who didn’t commit the crime. The case takes a turn when John meets a key witness who appears to recognise him - and not because he’s Ludwig. Is there more to this witness than meets the eye?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, Carol explores subjects that all begin with the letter T. Programmes include Gardeners' World, Coast, Alan Titchmarsh's Garden Secrets, The Edible Garden. With presenters Monty Don, Alan Titchmarsh, Rachel de Thame, Alys Fowler, Toby Buckland, Joe Swift and Carol Klein.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden flies above the green expanses of Hampshire, dropping in on two spectacular gardens. At Mottisfont, she meets a gardening veteran who's handing over the reins to his young protegee, and at the Sir Harold Hillier Garden, she learns about keeping it in the family. And she climbs into a pair of waders for some very unusual weeding.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek delves into Wales’s industrial past, including the slate trail in Gwyneddf and the Glo-Aur, a 17-mile walk to commemorate the Cymmer Mining Disaster, which claimed 114 lives.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: There are many ways to develop a fantastic garden while keeping costs down, and one of the most obvious ways is by taking cuttings from the plants you already have. With that in mind, Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson look at how to do so with various garden favourites - Brian with rhododendrons, and Kirsty with a range of tender perennials. Tender means they are vulnerable in the winter, so taking cuttings is also a great way of ensuring you have plants come the spring. Brian revisits his espaliered apple trees for more essential maintenance, and Kirsty sows hollyhocks for that cottage garden favourite next year. Kirsty also pays a visit to the new glasshouses at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, and there are all the usual weekly handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Hasan Semay brings his signature barbecue vibes into the studio with a classic Turkish Cypriot dish of lamb and potato koftes. Cynthia Shanmugalingam brings the flavours of Sri Lanka to the studio with her fiery prawn curry and coconut sambol. And to celebrate National Tequila Day, Carmen O’Neal has three cocktails to get any party started. Nadiya Hussain rustles up a fuss-free aubergine and feta tart, while Jane Baxter creates a classic cherry clafoutis with cherry ice cream and chocolate sauce. And finally, Tom Allen faces either his food heaven or his food hell. Meanwhile, Rick Stein takes to the high seas to fish for his supper, and the Hairy Bikers gleefully make and use ghee for their tasty tacos.

programme.title: Caribbean Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Four-part Caribbean cookery series in which passionate food enthusiast Levi Roots travels around Jamaica and across the UK showing how to bring sunshine flavours to your kitchen. Levi returns to Jamaica where he grew up to cook spicy lamb in his childhood village, eat delicious yam mash with the family of Jamaican Olympic hero Usain Bolt, and barbecue fish Caribbean style - on the beach.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. In this episode, Lorraine helps 26-year-old Bryony, who admits to passing shop-bought food off as her own but who has now been tasked with hosting her best friend's hen party. So Lorraine creates an inspiring canape menu for her, including Thai larb gai, bite-sized chocolate napoleons and delicate coconut meringues filled with ginger cream.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater creates a week's worth of simple-yet-delicious meals. In this episode, he transforms favourite classic recipes by giving them a new twist. Whether it's a makeover for the traditional cottage pie or an exciting new version of the time-honoured apple tart, Nigel proves that just by taking the basic principles and altering them slightly, it's easy to jazz up our most-loved dishes. Nigel also visits fellow passionate gardeners on allotments and gardens across the country, and creates the ultimate fresh feast from the fruits of their labour. This week, Nigel gives a new spin to beans on toast with newbie gardeners Karina and Craig. The series is part of the 'Dig In' campaign.

programme.title: Gymnastics: European Championships
programme.desc: Coverage of the men's team finals at the 2026 European Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb, Croatia.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: Coverage from the 2026 Diamond League meeting in Silesia, Poland.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Will two charming sketchbooks found in a garden shed in France finally be recognised as authentic works by French master Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec?

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: Having said goodbye to one pair, the six remaining teams of aspiring art dealers are tasked with buying and selling works to meet the brief of two high-end homeowners. Host Steph McGovern and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas are joined by Peter Staunton, an award-winning luxury interior designer who is on hand to tell the dealers about his clients’ tastes, as well as sharing tips and tricks when it comes to investing in art for the home.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 5 highlights from the Test match between England and Pakistan at Headingley.

programme.title: Blue Planet Revisited
programme.desc: A scattering of some 700 islands in the Atlantic Ocean, the Bahamas are home to one of the largest and most diverse shark populations on the planet. Over the course of three weeks, Steve Backshall discovers why the Bahamas provide such sanctuary for sharks, looking at the protection offered to them, people’s changing attitudes and the key role science plays in their conservation. Steve joins researchers who have dedicated their lives to this unique and often misunderstood group of animals and learns that a healthy shark population is absolutely vital to a healthy marine ecosystem.

programme.title: Why...?
programme.desc: After three recent fatal shark attacks in Egypt, this film investigates whether pressure from human activity and climate change is altering the behaviour of sharks.

programme.title: Jaws
programme.desc: When a great white shark begins preying on humans off the beaches of New England, a police chief, a shark expert and a grizzled fisherman head out on a perilous journey to hunt the creature down.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: With Brian’s family desperately seeking justice and answers, the fate of the accused hangs in the balance. Witnesses unearth more shocking revelations, and the defendant takes the stand before the jury answer the ultimate question: guilty or not guilty? As the police investigation team finally close in on their suspect, the court is shown dramatic footage from Campbell’s custody interview, where tempers flare when allegations are put to him. The prosecution point to a guilty man on the ropes, while the defence argue it shows a police force under pressure to get their man. As the case builds to a climax, with persuasive and gripping closing speeches from both sides, Campbell awaits his fate whilst Brian’s grieving family anxiously await justice – either way, lives will change forever.

programme.title: Buried with Michael Sheen
programme.desc: For years, Welsh actor Michael Sheen has been haunted by a story he discovered online about little-known farming consultant Douglas Gowan, who claimed the people of Wales had been poisoned by decades of toxic chemical dumping of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) - a known class 1 carcinogen often called the 'godfather of forever chemicals'. Unable to let the story go, Michael follows a toxic trail that leads him to ask: who’s in danger now? Search BBC Sounds to listen to the podcast Buried: The Last Witness, which the series is based on.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: With Michael living back at home and unemployed, he really can’t afford Linda anymore, so he decides to return her. Linda had made this week especially busy for Sue as it would have been her 50th wedding anniversary, so she leaves Michael with Sue’s itinerary and onward care instructions. But when Sue’s friends and Michael all let her down, she questions whether she can live without Linda.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Jason Manford presents the quiz where careful choices are everything, from Cats or The Lion King to Taxi or Bus, and even Margaret Thatcher or Theresa May. Only one team can swipe their way to victory.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The Bear Ladies fix an iconic mascot from the 1966 World Cup, Suzie repairs a well-travelled leather hat, and Pete and Sonnaz bring the music back to a battered old washboard.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of the day's matches on the opening weekend of the 2026/27 Premier League season, with new managers very much the focus. Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of Manchester City sees him take on Bournemouth, who are now led by Marco Rose. Bournemouth’s former manager Andoni Iraola takes his Liverpool team to Newcastle, who saw Eddie Howe leave in the summer to be replaced by Matthias Jaissle. By contrast, Unai Emery is now the second-longest serving Premier League manager behind Mikel Arteta. His Aston Villa team travel to Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts another five days of the quiz, with the action kicking off in Dundee. Traitors star Paul Gorton resumes his role as unreliable tour guide, mixing truths with tall tales as the celebrity players attempt to separate unbelievable facts from fiction. Comedian and presenter Susan Calman, internet star Max Fosh and DJ Noreen Khan are this week’s guests. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores carried forward throughout the week to decide the week's overall champion.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers have discovered lumps on the stomach of a zebra called Olivia. The vets perform surgery, but will Olivia survive the operation?

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: As everyone faces the final reckoning, the great river crossing begins. Gnu and Shani’s foal are tested by crocodiles. Duma must save his mother. Does Kali find happiness at last?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A Chinese vase brought to the Roadshow on a skateboard, an Italian super light dining chair, a French cabinet brought from the Caribbean on a banana boat and a large Buddha clad in gold leaf - it is an international mix when Michael Aspel and the experts visit Redruth in Cornwall.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin visits the beautiful Cotswolds village of Broadway to uncover its artistic past. He also revisits some of the historic venues from the series, with new valuations and unexpected auctions.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Jimi Famurewa, Harriet Kemsley, Colin Murray and Sara Pascoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s rail travels take him to the north west corner of France, where he explores the beautiful and historic regions of Brittany and Normandy and learns of their connections with Great Britain. He begins in Nantes, where he contends with the fantastical creatures that stalk the city’s former shipbuilding yards, among them a giant sloth, a vast spider and a huge heron. The mechanical monsters are inspired by the science fiction writing of Jules Verne, born in Nantes in 1828. At the castle of the dukes of Brittany, Michael discovers the city was once capital of the independent medieval Duchy of Brittany. He follows the trail of the region’s defiant defender, the Duchess Anne. On the tiny island of Gavrinis, in the Gulf of Morbihan, Michael investigates a rounded stone cairn, which conceals an elaborately decorated burial chamber built 6,000 years ago. At the port of Lorient, Michael discovers the enormous German submarine base from which the Nazis directed the Battle of the Atlantic during the Second World War.

This time, the specialist subjects in question are the Tour de France in the 21st century, singer-songwriter and member of The Beatles George Harrison, Virgil’s epic poem The Aeneid and the 36th president of the United States, Lyndon B Johnson.

His search leads him to Ruabon in north Wales, where many locals have voiced concerns about what they believe is a high incidence of cancer in the community. He also gets himself tested for PCB contamination in his own blood and brings together affected communities, scientists, environmentalists and politicians at the Welsh Parliament. Search BBC Sounds to listen to the podcast Buried: The Last Witness, which the series is based on.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the heart of the English countryside to fish a lake deep in the Surrey Hills, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. They hope to catch some carp and barbel - but will Bob's clumsiness stop them from catching these skittish fish? The two of them settle in for a chat about the joys of gardening, much to Paul's dismay. Later on, health expert Dr Anand Patel joins them by the lake. He and Bob dive straight into the importance of men looking after their health - especially their weight and particularly as they grow older.

programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.desc: In this unprecedented time of lockdown there has never been a better time to learn about the wildlife around us, and Deadly 60 fans have been sending in their videos, photos and questions for Steve Backshall to answer. In this episode, Steve focuses on our parks and gardens. This green space may look pristine, but for wildlife it’s savannah, jungle and mountains all rolled in to one. And judging by CBBC’s most observant viewers, its packed full of deadly animals! Steve unravels the mystery of some blue eggs in a nest, explains how a spider uses camouflage and trickery to lure in its prey, and tells about a worm that isn’t a worm... it’s a lizard! In a DIY demo, Steve then shows us how to keep hedgehogs warm and toasty during winter by building a hibernation house. But that’s not all. The audience gets their chance to ‘beat Backshall’ in a 60-second quickfire round. The question is, how many can Steve get right before his time is up? We also learn that fox cubs are endearing alarm clocks, and why you wouldn’t want to wander around an Australian garden without a grown-up!
